items.summary_original: In organisations today, data has never been more available. Dashboards and performance decks exist for almost every function — sales, product, marketing, operations — and the tools to build them have never been more accessible. And yet, in weekly standups and quarterly reviews, the same thing happens constantly: someone shares the numbers, the room nods, and the meeting ends without a decision or clear direction . When that happens, the data usually takes the blame. The numbers weren’t granular enough, the dataset wasn’t complete, we need more information before we can act. items.title: What Shakespeare got right about AI
items.summary_original: From ink and quill to glowing code: Shakespeare’s exploration of prophecy and equivocation, the art of speaking truths that mislead, anticipates the central challenge of our own relationship with artificial intelligence. Every warning we need about AI was written four hundred years ago. What witches, a forged letter, and a haunted prince can teach you about talking to a machine. The sharpest words ever written about artificial intelligence came from a man who never had electricity, a telephone, or a single line of code. He’s been dead four hundred years, and he still wrote thirty-seven plays about it. The obvious place to look for AI is science fiction, and plenty of people have gone looking. items.title_de: Was Shakespeare über KI richtig gemacht hat
items.summary_de: Von Tinte und Feder zum leuchtenden Code: Shakespeares Erforschung von Prophezeiung und Zweideutigkeit, der Kunst, irreführende Wahrheiten auszusprechen, nimmt die zentrale Herausforderung unserer eigenen Beziehung zur künstlichen Intelligenz vorweg. Jede Warnung, die wir über KI brauchen, wurde vor vierhundert Jahren geschrieben. Was Ihnen Hexen, ein gefälschter Brief und ein heimgesuchter Prinz über das Sprechen mit einer Maschine beibringen können. Die schärfsten Worte, die jemals über künstliche Intelligenz geschrieben wurden, kamen von einem Mann, der nie Strom, ein Telefon oder eine einzige Codezeile hatte. Er ist seit vierhundert Jahren tot und hat immer noch siebenunddreißig Stücke darüber geschrieben. Der offensichtliche Ort, an dem man nach KI suchen sollte, ist Science-Fiction, und viele Leute haben sich auf die Suche gemacht. Patrick Neeman hat einen guten Teil dieses Jahres damit verbracht, Star Wars, Matrix und Minority R zu benoten

items.title: IED master of arts graduates deploy design against the loss of common goods
items.summary_original: IED MASTERS of arts EVOLVE PRACTICE THROUGH DESIGN X COMMONS Marking an evolution in how design intervenes within contemporary society, the Master of Arts programs at Istituto Europeo di Design (IED) treat the discipline as a mediator between communities and common goods. Grounded in the understanding of commons as the material and immaterial resources that multiple communities engage with as the collective heritage of humanity, the overarching theme of Design X Commons elevates these graduate thesis projects past formal styling exercises and traditional product development. Combining research alongside speculative design strategies, the emerging designers confront climate vulnerability, urban privatization, labor exploitation, and spatial inequality to reshape collective urban futures. items.title: Captcha Design Festival
items.summary_original: Captcha is a design festival for watching, participating, and discussing. For everyone who wants to understand design not just as a finished product, but as an ongoing process. From September 14 to 21, 2026 , students from the Faculty of Design at Mannheim University of Applied Sciences will host the Captcha Design Festival , this year in cooperation with the City of Mannheim, the Abendakademie, and the Alte Feuerwache. Young designers in particular will be offered easy access to workshops and talks featuring exciting figures from the creative industry. This year’s Captcha is titled “Momentum.” Momentum refers to the momentum of an existing movement. It creates a momentum of its own that is virtually impossible to stop from the outside. Participants include A2 + B, Deutsche & Japaner, HAL

items.summary_original: rodolphe parente and marion mailaender reimagine ken club Rodolphe Parente and Marion Mailaender reimagine Paris’ Ken Club as an architecture in motion, bringing the 1985 identity of the fitness and social club into a contemporary setting opposite the Eiffel Tower . The architects approach the past as an architectural remix, shaping a place where the visual language and atmosphere of the 1980s are sampled, reworked, and given a new rhythm. Parente and Mailaender imagine the club almost as a film set built to last, recreating the atmosphere of another era without turning the interiors into a period replica. Saturated colors, rounded forms, reflective surfaces, and theatrical contrasts between light and shadow give the spaces a sense of movement. all images by Mathias Benguigui, unless state

Guinness has a new campaign out, and before you've even looked at it, you may be wondering why the design press always gives this brand so much attention. Well, the answer has some quite deep historical roots. The Irish stout brand actually didn't advertise at all for the first 170 years of its history. Its strict philosophy was that the quality of the beer alone should do the talking. After the end of the First World War, though, a slump in sales meant the family that owned the company finally relented. Und tief in Ihrem Inneren wissen Sie, dass, ganz gleich, welche cleveren und wirkungsvollen Designs Sie auch erstellen, mindestens einer von ihnen fragen wird: „Können Sie unser Logo etwas größer machen?“ Das ist so ziemlich das Szenario, mit dem eine Londoner Kreativagentur möglicherweise konfrontiert war, als British Cycling an sie herantrat, um an ihrer National Series und National Championships zu arbeiten. „Und weil Lloyds der Hauptpartner ist“, sagt Kreativdirektor Alex Andlaw. „Wir mussten Lloyds und British Cycling auch ohne das gleiche Gewicht geben.“

items.title: Why Studio Kiln swapped Cornwall for London
items.summary_original: The award-winning studio has spent years proving creativity doesn't need a postcode. So why are they now heading for the Big Smoke? Even in 2026, some people get sniffy about the idea of running a design studio outside of London. Especially somewhere like Falmouth, 300 miles away on the west coast of England. And yet that's exactly where Studio Kiln decided to set up shop, back in 2022. And since then, it's all gone surprisingly well. The creative practice has won a number of awards and built a strong reputation for its branding and digital work, such as its particle system for BAFTA . It's all powerful proof that you don't need to be anywhere near the M25 to prosper. So our ears pricked up when we heard, recently, that the studio was taking on space in London.
